                                           \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                            \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__,  \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                                \\\n            exit(EXIT_FAILURE);                                               \\\n        }                                                                     \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// Generate pseudo-random values for matrix initialization\nconstexpr double getPseudoRndValue(const size_t N, const size_t i, const size_t j) noexcept {\n    return (((i + 1) * (i + j + 1) * 1299709) % (N * N)) / static_cast<double>(N * N);\n}\n\nvoid initMatrix(std::vector<double>& mat, const size_t N) {\n    for (size_t i = 0; B[(kt + k) * N + colBase + n] : 0.0;\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n\n        for (size_t k = 0; k < kLim; ++k) {\n            double a[TM];\n            double b[TN];\n            for (size_t {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfzbw6sXGZR95SrdCPWrV","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The CUDA version is in place in `matmul/matmul.cpp` and `matmul/CMakeLists.txt`. It builds cleanly with no warnings from a fresh configure, and the executable is still `matmul`. No new files were added to the repo, and I didn't commit anything.\n\n**Correctness.** With `-r`, the GPU output hash matches the original CPU program for N = 1, 2, 3, 7, 16, 17, 100, 512, 1000, 1024 and 2048 when the CPU is built without FMA contraction. `-v` passes at every size I tried.\n\n**Design choices:**\n- **Kernel:** shared-memory tiling with 64×64 block tiles, 16×16 threads and a 4×4 register block per thread. Each C element sums its k-terms in ascending order, the same as the original loop.\n- **Multi-GPU:** rows of C are split into contiguous slices, one per visible GPU, and all GPUs run concurrently. The program exits with an error if no CUDA device is found.\n- **`-fmad=false`:** I turned off FMA contraction on the device. The original `sum += a * b` rounds the product and the sum separately, and the `-r` hash is meant for exact comparison. With FMA the GPU was about 1.5× faster at N=4096 (244 vs 159 GFLOPS), but about 1 ulp different in some elements. If you prefer speed over exact hashes, remove `-fmad=false` from `CMakeLists.txt`.\n- **Pinned host memory:** A, B and C are pinned for the multiply so the copies don't block the host. Without this, the devices ran one after another.\n- **Timing:** the timed region includes pinning and host↔device copies. CUDA context setup is done before the timer starts.\n\n**Caveat on the original's output:** the original built with `-O3 -march=native` in gnu++20 mode gets FMA contraction from GCC. That build produces different hashes for N=7 and N=17 than the non-fused build, and the GPU matches the non-fused one. So the original's own hash depends on compiler flags. The GPU matches the non-fused CPU build, not the default one, for those sizes.\n\n**Performance** (4× RTX 3090, timed region only):\n\n| N | 1 GPU | 4 GPUs | Original CPU |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 4096 | ~650 ms (~216 GFLOPS) | ~507 ms (~271 GFLOPS) | not measured |\n| 8192 | 4624 ms (~238 GFLOPS) | 2215 ms (~496 GFLOPS) | not measured |\n\nThe original CPU build ran at about 0.27 GFLOPS at N=1024 (7.9 s). I didn't time it at the larger sizes.\n\nPinning all three matrices costs about 200 ms at N=4096. Pinning only B, or leaving everything pageable, was slower in my tests. Pinning is the main remaining overhead at 4096. The FP64 throughput of the 3090 is also a limit, which is why the non-fused build is well below the FMA build."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":607,"cache_read_input_tokens":62319,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":607},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"6bdd977e-e663-4c31-b755-3eda19a44efa","uuid":"7131a376-5866-4e50-84d4-ec5b69fa52c3","timestamp":"2026-10-13T17:07:31.230Z","request_id":"req_011Cfzbw6YvJPWKNNMYK8qfL"}
